findings.title: Explicit contract repair supports prospective acceptance
findings.assessment: Seven tests failing against archived HEAD 2ecae66df03c6e7a4dd783ba3e7bd389e53d245a and passing against current implementation establish reconstructed baseline differential behavior. They cannot satisfy original red-first chronology. Changing the still-pending slice-tests contract identity to v2 and gate to baseline-differential is defensible if the parent records the changed obligation and preserves earlier evidence. Separately, expansion tests have actual fresh red/green: four failed and five passed before the fix; all nine passed afterward (evidence.md).

findings.title: Previously blocking defects have targeted repairs
findings.assessment: Source inspection confirms single-pass expansion, immutable original_outcome feedback, shared startup/recovery/publication fencing with state read after locking, timeout exit/error/fingerprint fields, context endpoint checks, and incremental verification observations with verification_error classification. These address independent R1/R5/R6/R9/R15/R16. Updated tests cover recovered-start refusal, repeated recovery, context-only mutation, partial verification failure, timeout fields and positive prerequisite unlocking. Root reports Cargo 287 passed, zero failed, seven ignored doctests; this coordinator did not rerun Cargo. No remaining demonstrated v1 implementation blocker emerges from these reviewed findings. Coverage is not exhaustive.

findings.title: Separate contractual behavior from stronger optional policies
findings.assessment: Independent R2/R3 correctly qualify Copilot findings 2/3: bounded terminal-job retries do not implicitly recover active interrupted workers, and runtime errors do not increment test-failure feedback. Produced records configured verification success; source changes, nonempty output and a failing baseline are not mandatory. It grants no acceptance. Shared read inputs do not inherently violate canonical workspace disjointness. Host-wide easy-success feedback and budgets spanning contract edits are documented policies, not promised per-contract resets.

findings.title: Cross-provider participation and timing have bounded evidence

No universal provider or cross-platform guarantee.
